definitions.explanation: The sink area in a kitchen, including the basin and the surrounding counter space used for washing dishes and food preparation.
A taxi driving around without a passenger, looking to pick someone up. Also used for street musicians or performers who move from place to place.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}しに{皿|さら}を{置|お}く。
examples.english: I put the plates in the sink.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}しの{排水口|はいすいこう}が{詰|つ}まってしまった。
examples.english: The kitchen sink drain got clogged.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{終|お}わった{食器|しょっき}は{流|なが}しに{持|も}っていってね。
examples.english: Please bring the used dishes to the sink when you're done eating.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}しのタクシーを{拾|ひろ}う。
この{辺|あた}りは{流|なが}しのタクシーが{多|おお}いので、すぐ{捕|つか}まる。
examples.english: There are many cruising taxis around here, so you can catch one quickly.

examples.japanese: {流|なが}しの{演奏家|えんそうか}が{店|みせ}を{回|まわ}って{歌|うた}っていた。
examples.english: A roaming musician was going around shops singing.

notes: Derived from the verb {流|なが}す (to let flow). For sense 1, the word originally referred to the drain channel in traditional Japanese kitchens. In modern usage, {台所|だいどころ}の{流|なが}し specifically means the kitchen sink. The more technical term is {流|なが}し{台|だい} (sink unit/counter). For sense 2, {流|なが}しのタクシー is the standard phrase for a taxi looking for fares on the street, as opposed to one waiting at a taxi stand ({駅前|えきまえ}のタクシー{乗|の}り{場|ば}).
